rows.figure: another five receive emergency department care (per child drowning death)
rows.scope: Children: emergency-department visits for nonfatal submersion injuries per child drowning death, United States, as stated on CDC's 'Unintentional Drowning: Get the Facts' page (page last updated 24 October 2014). The sentence says only 'child'; the sentence before it concerns children 14 and younger. Data years are not stated for the ratio: its reference (1) is WISQARS, 'cited 2012 May 3'. The page's death counts are for 2005–2009, but the ratio is not tied to those years.
rows.source: CDC, National Center for Injury Prevention and Control, 'Unintentional Drowning: Get the Facts' (Water-Related Injuries Facts), page last updated 24 October 2014; Wayback Machine capture of 23 December 2014 (timestamp 20141223054643)
rows.do_not_add_to: A ratio for one age group and one door (emergency department) with unstated data years: never averaged with cdc-children-nonfatal-ed-7 (CDC's later 'another 7'), with the all-ages or adult ratios (cdc-nonfatal-ed-2012-2021, ontario-nonfatal-ed-ratio-2014-2023, australia-nonfatal-hospitalisation-ratio-2002-2015) or turned into a count; never cited as a global ratio.
rows.note: The sentence as printed: 'For every child who dies from drowning, another five receive emergency department care for nonfatal submersion injuries.' followed by reference 1 (WISQARS). Superseded on CDC's site by 'another 7' (row cdc-children-nonfatal-ed-7). This is the primary behind the 'five times' figure that Felton et al. 2015, Safe Kids 2016 and many state fact sheets repeat. Read in the built-in browser from the Wayback Machine capture of 23 Dec 2014.

evidence.quote: another five receive emergency department care for nonfatal submersion injuries

The Wayback Machine capture of 23 December 2014 of CDC's 'Unintentional Drowning: Get the Facts' page, whose footer says 'Page last updated: October 24, 2014', prints: 'For every child who dies from drowning, another five receive emergency department care for nonfatal submersion injuries.' with reference 1, which is WISQARS 'cited 2012 May 3'. So the acceptance point 'the data years the ratio covers, as the page states them' has a definite answer: the page states none for the ratio; the only years on the page are 2005–2009 for the death counts (reference 2, MMWR 2012;61(19):344–347), and the ratio is not tied to them. The row is graded A as CDC's own page in an archived copy. Nothing changes for cdc-children-nonfatal-ed-7 except that the five-to-seven change now has a dated earlier endpoint; the archive.cdc.gov follow-up would date the switch. The page's capture is the version Felton et al. 2015 cite (24 October 2014). No names recorded: the page's reference list names authors of cited papers, which were not transcribed.
